label: First copy step (echo of orig token 0) when the sequence starts 3/r/d followed by r,t,e,j,f,c,o then j,t,r,o,e,k,f,a
explanation: Fires only at recall_idx==1: the first copy step after <DEL>, where the input is the echoed first original token and the output is orig(1). It is 100% of activation mass and it never fires in the original or delimiter phases. Within that step it is a sparse conjunction over the first three original tokens. The first token is mostly 3, r or d (87% of mass; c and f are weaker). orig(1) favors r/t/e/j/f/c/o and orig(2) favors j/t/r/o/e/k/f/a. The strongest activations are on sequences starting with 3 (for example 3 o j..., 3 c t..., 3 t j). It looks like a thresholded additive combination of token identities, not a crisp set rule. Even the 3-token conjunction has low precision, and many sequences with matching tokens stay inactive. Magnitude is narrow (0.10-0.19) and is highest for first token 3 with orig(1) and orig(2) both in the preferred sets.
